Subject: Re: MSA edits + Exhibit E capacity mapping — initial sync

Karthik —

Got the packet, thanks. Quick notes from Legal: they want to keep the term length at 12 months but are open to a pricing tier for committed sustained capacity. They redlined the vendor indemnity clause (section 6) and flagged the data-retention sentence for our Security team to confirm. Procurement asked if you can accept net-45 on the initial term (we can escalate if needed).

I’ll loop in our Security and Procurement contacts in a follow-up if that’s helpful. For now: can your legal ops provide a short memo explaining the proposed term-change rationale (why a 24-month option is better from a capacity/price tradeoff)? That will help speed internal approval.

—Jenna
Sr. Counsel, Nimbus Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 May 2028 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA edits + Exhibit E capacity mapping — legal gap map (see memo)

Jenna —

Appreciate the quick read. Looping in Lauren (Legal Ops) and Grace (Renewals) to draft the memo and address Procurement’s net-45 ask. Summary below and attached as two slides:

• Why 24 months helps Nimbus: predictability for model provisioning (reduces risk of short-term spikes causing throttling), enables discounted reserved capacity, and reduces unit price by ~14% on the Exhibit E profile.
• Term mechanics we propose: 24-month base with an early-exit clause tied to material breach or failure to meet SLA for two consecutive months (we included the SLA language as plain text in the redline).
• Indemnity: we can accept limited indemnity for third-party IP claims but need to cap at aggregate of fees paid in prior 12 months; our Legal Ops will propose language.

Attachments: NIMBUS_MSA_v3_redline.pdf (annotated comments), ExhibitE_capacity_table.xlsx, 20280509-term-memo.pdf

Lauren / Grace — can you prioritize a short memo and proposed indemnity clause by EOD tomorrow? Procurement wants a strawman before their internal pricing committee meets next week.

Thanks —
Karthik

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@nimbushealth.com>, Alex Cohen <alex.cohen@nimbushealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 May 2028 16:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA edits + Exhibit E capacity mapping — final gap map + next steps

Hi Jenna / Alex —

Attached is a concise gap map that pairs each of your redline bullets with our proposed language and rationale. Key highlights:

1) Term / Pricing — We propose a 24-month committed term with a one-time option to convert to 12-month rolling after month 12 with 60 days' notice; this provides Nimbus with budgetary flexibility while preserving reserved capacity economics.

2) Indemnity — Proposed limit: aggregate fees paid during prior 12 months, capped at $2M, carve-outs for gross negligence and willful misconduct.

3) Data-retention — We clarified the retention window and included the SOC2 attestation link for your Security team to validate.

4) Billing cadence — Accepting net-45 for the first renewal cycle only; subsequent cycles revert to net-30 unless Procurement requests otherwise in writing.

Attachments: gap-map_Nimbus_20280512.pdf, NIMBUS_MSA_v3_redline.pdf, ExhibitE_capacity_table.xlsx

Next steps:
- If the gap map looks acceptable, please confirm by EOD Mon 05/15 and we’ll prepare a clean MSA for signature routing.
- If Procurement needs alternate PO language, send a 1-paragraph example and we’ll fold it into the final.

Best —
Lauren Bishop
Legal Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
